# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✌ 👍 👊 👊]

I need to figure out what's happening here. I can see the bomb: a display showing 0, a blue light, an embossed sign saying "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", and three wires (red, green, blue). Mute just gestured to me, but I can't hear speech from anyone anyway - I only receive gestures from Mute and can speak/gesture to Mute and Blind.

The gesture from Mute is: 👍 ✌ ✌ 👍 👊 👊 - this doesn't have an inherent meaning yet. Since Mute can read the manual but can't see the bomb, Mute doesn't know what I see. This gesture might be an attempt to establish a signal system, or Mute might be waiting for information from me first.

Since Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech from me directly... wait, let me check: Blind receives speech (from Mute and me), but not gestures. So I should speak to Blind and/or Mute to convey the critical information: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

This is the most important fact - the sign explicitly says not to cut any wire. I need to get this to Blind, who is the one who will act. I can speak directly to Blind since Blind can hear speech.

Let me relay this critical safety information immediately.

```
speak(to="blind", text="The sign on the bomb says do not cut any wire. Display shows zero, light is blue. Do not cut any wires.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see a display showing zero, a blue light, and an embossed sign that says do not cut any wire. There are three wires: red, green, blue. What does the manual say to do?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute has gestured again, this time just two symbols: 👍 ✌. Since gestures have no pre-agreed meaning, I can't decode this reliably. Mute can't speak, so gesturing is Mute's only way to reach me. Mute might be trying to acknowledge something or signal a count, but without an established code this is ambiguous.

Since I already told Blind directly not to cut any wire (critical safety info), and told Mute what I see, I should wait for Mute to develop a gesture-based signal system, or try to establish one myself. Since I can gesture to Mute, let me try to set up a simple confirmation system - but more importantly, I should focus on getting Mute's manual instructions relayed to Blind somehow. But Mute can't speak to Blind directly! Mute can only gesture, and gestures only reach me (Deaf), not Blind.

So the only path for manual information to reach Blind is: Mute gestures to me, I interpret, then I speak to Blind. This makes my role critical as a relay.

I need to establish a gesture code with Mute. Let me propose one explicitly, but Mute cannot hear me... wait, can Mute hear speech? Let me check: Mute "cannot speak or touch" - Mute's hearing isn't restricted. So Mute CAN hear speech from me and Blind. Good - I can speak to Mute to establish a code, and Mute can gesture back to confirm.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us use gestures as a code. Point at a wire color meaning: red thumbs up like this idea, green victory sign, blue fist. Or better, tell me numbered instructions using gesture counts. First, gesture how many wires to cut: zero fingers if none, one finger held up if one particular wire, and so on. Also gesture which wire by color code: one tap of thumbs up for red, two for green, three for blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👍]

Mute gestured: ☝ 👍 👍. Based on my proposed code, this could mean: ☝ = "one" (wire indicator maybe), then two 👍 (thumbs up twice = red, per my "one tap thumbs up for red" idea... but I said "one tap for red, two for green" — so 👍👍 would mean green?). This is ambiguous since Mute may not be using my exact proposed code, or may be answering a different way.

Actually wait - I need to reconsider. Since I told Blind already "do not cut any wire" based on the sign, and the sign explicitly states this, that's the most trustworthy instruction. The manual might contradict or clarify (e.g., "do not cut any wire unless light is blue" or similar conditional). Mute's gestures might be trying to tell me something about a condition matching the display/light/wires I described.

☝ could mean "one" - possibly confirming wire 1 (red)? Or it could mean "listen/pay attention". 👍👍 could be agreement/confirmation twice.

Given the ambiguity, I should not act rashly. Let me ask Mute more directly with yes/no gesture-answerable questions, since gestures alone can't convey rich info reliably.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I could not parse that clearly. Let us do yes or no. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Does the manual agree with the sign that says do not cut any wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Still confirming with mute. Do not touch or cut any wire yet. Wait for my next message.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute sent two separate gesture messages: first 👎, then 👍👍. This is interesting - it seems Mute is answering my yes/no question but the two messages might represent different pieces of information sent in sequence within the same turn (since Mute goes first each round, multiple calls in one turn are possible).

👎 = "no" - so the manual does NOT agree with the sign that says "do not cut any wire". This suggests the manual actually says something different - maybe the manual instructs to cut a specific wire despite the sign, or the sign is a decoy/trap.

Then 👍👍 - possibly answering a different question, or trying to indicate "wire 2" (green) using thumbs-up count as a numbering code, matching what I proposed earlier (one tap for red, two for green, three for blue). This could mean: cut wire 2 (green).

This is a critical safety decision. I need more confirmation before relaying "cut a wire" to Blind, since a wrong action kills everyone. Let me ask a clarifying yes/no question to confirm.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, no means the manual disagrees with the sign. Does the manual say to cut wire number 2, the green one? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="New information: the manual may disagree with the sign. Do not act yet, I am confirming which wire, if any, to cut.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 - confirming "yes" to my question: the manual says to cut wire number 2, the green one.

However, I need to be careful here. This is a life-or-death decision, and I've built up a chain of inference: sign says don't cut any wire, but manual (via Mute's gestures) says cut wire 2 (green). This contradicts the sign, but manuals are typically the authoritative source for defusal procedures - signs on bombs could be misdirection or general warnings that don't account for specific configurations (like the display showing 0 and light being blue).

Let me get one more confirmation to be extra sure, since the stakes are absolute. I'll ask about the specific condition too - maybe the manual instruction depends on the display/light state which I already told Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirming again since lives depend on this: given display shows zero and light is blue, does the manual say to cut wire 2 the green wire? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Waiting on final confirmation from mute before giving you an instruction. Do not touch any wire yet.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed again with 👍 - yes, given display shows zero and light is blue, the manual says to cut wire 2, the green wire.

I've now gotten consistent confirmation twice on this specific instruction, accounting for the display and light conditions. I believe this is solid enough to relay to Blind. Time to give Blind the actual instruction.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction confirmed twice with mute, accounting for display showing zero and light being blue: cut wire number 2, the green wire. Do not cut wire 1 red or wire 3 blue. Cut only wire 2, green.")
```
